Comparing [v7.2.0 against v7.3.0](https://github.com/mui/material-ui/compare/v7.2.0...v7.3.0), I don't see any changes to Autocomplete other than https://github.com/mui/material-ui/commit/472cc721ccb96a79dbf362cea3f6cd269e11be2a#diff-a3e15b1f22a8ed2de23c8cee46ea92a1d2828d4718cb471c6404d9baadd2c68f

We're seeing the same behavior in our app with MUI v7.3+ without Playwright. Downgrading to v7.2.0 fixed the issue. I will try to create a reproduction repo

I was able to reproduce it here: https://stackblitz.com/edit/zl8qpkqz?file=src%2FDemo.tsx,package.json

To reproduce: enter any text in the text field and blur out of the field. The value should be whatever text you entered but will stay undefined.

The behavior is triggered when the `options` array is empty and `autoHighlight` is set to `true`.

The bug was introduced with v7.3.0. Downgrading to v7.2.0 fixes it.
Since the issue is missing key information and has been inactive for 7 days, it has been automatically closed. If you wish to see the issue reopened, please provide the missing information.

Thanks for posting a reproducable example and for letting me know that I am not the only one who can not use MUI >=7.3 because of regressions.

I am not sure why the bot has immediatelly closed the issue again, lets hope a reply will change its mind.

It is related to #46489, but that shouldn't be the regression because it actually found the wrong usage of the `freeSolo + autoHighlight` prop combination. The reason is the same as https://github.com/mui/material-ui/issues/46729#issuecomment-3216538809:

> Using `freeSolo` together with `autoHighlight` doesn’t really make sense. If the intent is to allow arbitrary input (`freeSolo`), then automatically highlighting the first matching option contradicts that behavior.

Thank you for your reply @ZeeshanTamboli 

In our case, the autocompete is used for selecting from an existing set of options as well as for creating a new entry in that set so auto highlighting the first match might be useful so that the user doesn't try to recreate an already existing entry.

> In our case, the autocompete is used for selecting from an existing set of options as well as for creating a new entry in that set so auto highlighting the first match might be useful so that the user doesn't try to recreate an already existing entry.

@olivier-lxo So why is your options array empty in the provided reproduction?
It is initially empty when the user first onboards. The user will then add entries to it over time.

@olivier-lxo You are right. It should work with freeSolo + autoHighlight even when there are no options so that you can add them later and enable highlighting first option. Since it used to work before it's a regression from #46489. I'll try to fix this in #46894.
Sounds great. Thank you!

comments.body:
Here's a guide on what I've been doing to add these:

1. If the component doesn't have an .e2e file, create one with the template from above.
2. Modify the sass path, validate it's correct
3. Modify the component import
4. Render the component into a default state 
   - For this I've been looking at the storybook stories and picking out the most general/simple one and essentially copying it over to the test file.
   - Be sure to render all the different component state/display variants (size props, type/kind props, checked, open/close etc)
5. Remove any unnecessary code relating to the story (bx/prefix code, extraneous components, state wrappers, etc)
6. Add some type of unique text content to the component so it's easily queryable for interactions
7. Modify the 'should render' `it` block with an appropriate query
8. Add any additional test blocks for component interaction variants (checked, open/closed, etc)
9. `cd` into `packages/react` and run `yarn cypress open-ct`
    - this will open the cypress gui in a new instance of chrome where you can select and run tests, and view the UI it's snapshotting and testing against.
10. Make any modifications needed, save and PR 🎉 
11. Ensure percy status check UI shows the component has an associated snapshot. This may require approval in the Percy UI

Helpful links I've referenced along the way:

- [Cypress' `viewport()` documentation](https://docs.cypress.io/api/commands/viewport)
- [Cypress' assertion documentation](https://docs.cypress.io/guides/references/assertions)
- [Overview of the `@testing-library/cypress` package](https://testing-library.com/docs/cypress-testing-library/intro/) that provides RTL-style queries in cypress tests
- [List of examples of all RTL-style queries](https://github.com/testing-library/cypress-testing-library/blob/97939da7d4707a71049884c0324c0eda56e26fc2/cypress/integration/find.spec.js) made available by the `@testing-library/cypress` package
Closing. We've migrated away from cypress to instead use playwright and added baseline VRT snapshots for all components in https://github.com/carbon-design-system/carbon/pull/11302

candidates.title: [Bug Report][3.1.4] v-text-field - change event not handled by component (Vuetify 2 regression)
candidates.origin: repo:vuetifyjs/vuetify is:issue is:closed regression in:title (batch-fourteen query cap)
candidates.reason: Vuetify2->3 framework change/payload contract, no same-framework working pair.
candidates.issueBody:
### Environment
**Vuetify Version:** 3.1.4
**Last working version:** 2.6.14
**Vue Version:** 3.2.47
**Browsers:** Chrome 109.0.0.0
**OS:** Windows 10

### Steps to reproduce
In Vuetify 2, one could use the `change` event on v-text-field to mimic the behavior of the .lazy modifier on `input` HTML elements.

In Vuetify 3, v-text-field no longer has specific handling for `change`, so it instead falls to the HTML `input` element and receives an `Event` as a payload, rather than the value of the text field like it did in Vuetify 2.

### Expected Behavior
`change` event on v-text-field is emitted with the text field's value

### Actual Behavior
`change` event on v-text-field is emitted with the raw Event object

### Reproduction Link
[https://play.vuetifyjs.com/#...](https://play.vuetifyjs.com/#)

candidates.origin: repo:palantir/blueprint is:issue is:closed regression in:title (batch-fourteen query cap)
candidates.reason: Popover2 new-component styling compared to other API, no same-package working-release keyboard criterion established.
candidates.issueBody:
`react-popper` adds an extra wrapper tag:

https://github.com/souporserious/react-popper/blob/ef520ee1213f30d3af3f10c6f5b4a04a888deb73/src/Manager.jsx#L36

**But**

`.pt-button-group` expects its **direct children** to be `.pt-button` or `.pt-popover-target` : 
https://github.com/palantir/blueprint/blob/dd90bfa0943dd6ac2ea1d233162cc3c21aa4e701/packages/core/src/components/button/_button-group.scss#L102-L116

Setting `rootElementTag` to `false`, which should remove `react-popper`'s Manager's wrapper does not work:

```
invariant.js:44 Uncaught Error: Manager.render(): A valid React element (or null) must be returned. You may have returned undefined, an array or some other invalid object.
```

It's because `children` is an array of 2 React components:

https://github.com/palantir/blueprint/blob/dd90bfa0943dd6ac2ea1d233162cc3c21aa4e701/packages/labs/src/components/popover/popover2.tsx#L268-L288

https://github.com/souporserious/react-popper/blob/ef520ee1213f30d3af3f10c6f5b4a04a888deb73/src/Manager.jsx#L38-L40

Of course I hacked something in my own project and Popover2 is in Lab so I have no expectation or need for this getting fixed before it is moved to Core to replace Popover for `2.0`.

Thanks for the great work, as usual!

comments.body: @marcoamonteiro this is a very old issue and it refers to an old version of Popover2. If you are experiencing a similar problem now with `@blueprintjs/popover2`, please file a new issue.

candidates.origin: repo:palantir/blueprint is:issue is:closed regression in:title (batch-fourteen query cap)

candidates.issueBody:
Hi guys!

I got a regression in updating from 1.1.0 to 1.2.0 (latest).

The bug comes from [this PR](https://github.com/palantir/blueprint/pull/297).

The component crashes during its instantiation because of [this change](https://github.com/palantir/blueprint/pull/297/files#diff-2899fd9fc14d599c6e4062f791d99120L135).

Some screenshots:

![screen shot 2016-12-09 at 00 47 57](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/591804/21040618/b87be8aa-bdab-11e6-9766-0734501da2a1.png)

![screen shot 2016-12-09 at 00 47 24](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/591804/21040620/bbc5d106-bdab-11e6-9b19-c6de34328d76.png)

It worked before to pass a `string` to the component because of the `moment(date)`.

Now it doesn't work anymore because of the `moment([date.getFullYear(), ...])`.

To be honest, your doc says that `value` should be a `Date` and not a `string`, so...

We could indicate in the changelog the potential breaking change and a possible solution, e.g.

> replacing `value={value}` by `value={new Date(value)}`

Or maybe a workaround in the code to keep the previous behaviour?

candidates.issueBody: (Mac OS Mojave 10.14.4, Chrome 74.0.3729.157) It looks like more complex `data-content` for a [Popover](https://getbootstrap.com/docs/4.3/components/popovers/) is not rendered correctly. For example, these two spans with a popover ([fiddle](https://jsfiddle.net/awjLxzhv/1/)): ```html POP POP ``` work fine with [v4.2.1](https://usebootstrap.com/cdn/4.2.1) ![popover-4 2 1](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/12053937/58236268-e2297180-7d85-11e9-958d-c1dc359c1589.jpg) but the button in the Popover disappear when I switch to [v4.3.2](https://usebootstrap.com/cdn/4.3.1) ![popover-4 3 1](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/12053937/58236278-e6ee2580-7d85-11e9-9798-b99f32c8e4b3.jpg) This seems to be the case with input elements in general, whereas text in `p` and `span` shows up ok.

comments.body:
Hi @jenstroeger,

That's the correct behavior and you'll find why by reading that: https://blog.getbootstrap.com/2019/02/13/bootstrap-4-3-1-and-3-4-1/

And you'll find how to fix that behavior here: https://getbootstrap.com/docs/4.3/getting-started/javascript/#sanitizer

BTW it's a good practice to read changelogs when you update any libs 👍
@Johann-S, ugh, yes I missed that. All fixed and working now again, thank you 👍🏼

candidates.title: Popover positioning regression
candidates.origin: repo:twbs/bootstrap is:issue is:closed regression in:title (batch-fourteen query cap)
candidates.issueBody:
I built multi-level menu using Bootstrap 4 popovers. It worked like a harm with Popper 1.12.6 (Bootstrap 4-beta2), but since 1.12.7 menu positioning is broken. Tested with all versions including 1.13.0-next, and Bootstrap 4.0.

Looks like the second-level popover is placed incorrectly. It works if I use Bootstrap 4.0 with Popper 1.12.6.

https://codepen.io/anon/pen/mpYmVX

I've found out that removing my `.popover-body { overflow-x: hidden; }` fixes the issue, but I need the popover scrollable.

I created also https://github.com/FezVrasta/popper.js/issues/532, but I can't provide Popper-only test case.

comments.body: We'll have to look into why we're including that overflow.

Sorry if I wasn't clear. That overflow style is added by my custom css not Bootstrap. However, I think it's a valid use-case even if you didn't think about popovers containing buttons that open another popovers before.

I also have a popover placement issue from popper 1.12.7
Still broken with popper 1.12.9
1.12.6 works well

After few investigation, it seems that if the element triggering the popover has a container with an overflow set to scroll or hidden and the popover doesn't have enough space to position itself in the container with the right placement then the popover rollback to an unexpected position.

Bootstrap 4.0.0 + popper 1.12.9 + container with overflow set to scroll > unexpected position
https://codepen.io/anon/pen/RxXKgY

Bootstrap 4.0.0 + popper 1.12.6 + container without overflow > expected position
https://codepen.io/anon/pen/opKBQM
Created a new Popper ticket with simpler test case https://github.com/FezVrasta/popper.js/issues/535

A workaround is to set `boundary: 'window'` (or 'viewport') in popover config. Maybe this should become a default for popover if Popper.js does not fix the issue on their side. For more see https://github.com/FezVrasta/popper.js/issues/535

@Johann-S you think you can fix that, or you rather wait for @FezVrasta for an opinion?

@ tompat you helped me bro.
With the sroll issue, working as expected

@alecpl we have boundary option in our Popover/Tooltip plugins see : https://getbootstrap.com/docs/4.0/components/popovers/#options

Is it still an issue ?
As I said before it works with `boundary: 'window'`, but not with default settings.
@mdo this issue can be solve if folks use `boundary: 'window'` for their Popovers but not sure if it's enough to close this issue 🤔

This happens because Popper.js considers as boundary element the closest `overflow !== initial` parent, this because in most of the cases this will make any popper get cut out by the parent.

We may improve the way the boundary element is detected to better detect this specific case where the `overflow !== initial` is not actually going to cut out a `position: absolute` popper.

https://github.com/FezVrasta/popper.js/issues/611
I'll close this issue, because there is a solution using `boundary: window`
